title: Elena Hardy finds GLI3 mutation in the NCBI data

tellings.quote: There's a mutation in one of those genes called GLI3, where a similar kind of mutation is associated in the literature with polysyndactyly.

plain: Genetic data from the small three-fingered mummies found near Nazca, Peru, shows a mutation in a gene called GLI3, according to the researcher Elena Hardy, who looked at the data herself in NCBI, a public US database of genetic information. She tells Michels that a similar mutation is linked in the scientific literature to polysyndactyly, a condition of extra or fused fingers and toes. That could offer an explanation for the bodies' unusual hands.
